help.exec.lead: A shell running in Windows, in its own window beside the screen. Windows has to be running.
help.exec.step1: Click Terminal (>_) in the toolbar. A PowerShell tab opens in your Windows home folder.
help.exec.step2: Option-click or right-click Terminal to pick another shell, or another folder to start in.
help.exec.step3: Press ⌘T in the Terminal window for another tab.
help.exec.note.title: Runs as Administrator
help.exec.note.body: Every shell has full rights in Windows, so there is no separate run-as-administrator step.
help.exec.fig.terminal.alt: The Terminal window with a PowerShell tab, after running a command in Windows
help.files.lead: Files in Windows is a window that works like Finder, for Windows' own folders. Windows has to be running.
help.files.step1: Click Files in Windows in the toolbar.
help.files.step2: To copy to Windows, drop files from Finder onto the window. They go into the folder you're looking at, or into a folder you drop them on.
help.files.step3: To copy to your Mac, drag files out of the window into Finder, or right-click them and choose Copy to Mac…
help.files.note.title: Nothing is replaced
help.files.note.body: A file with the same name stays as it is, and the copy gets a number. To work on a Mac folder from Windows without copying, share it in Details, under Shared folder.
help.files.fig.files.alt: The Files window showing a Windows folder, with its places on the left
help.save.lead: A checkpoint keeps the whole machine as it is now: open programs, memory and disk. Take one before something risky. Windows has to be running.
help.save.step1: Click Checkpoints (the clock) in the toolbar, then New Checkpoint.
help.save.step2: Give it a name, or leave the name empty and it's named by the time.
help.save.step3: Quicker: Option-click or right-click the clock and choose Take a Checkpoint Now.
help.save.note.title: Automatic checkpoints
help.save.note.body: winvm also takes some itself: one when this machine first starts, one when you leave Windows idle for a while, and one when it's put away. Automatic, in the Checkpoints view, shows or hides them.
help.save.fig.new.alt: The Checkpoints view with New Checkpoint asking for a name, over the cards of earlier checkpoints
help.restore.lead: Now, the large card at the bottom, is Windows as it is. Older checkpoints sit above it, and the timeline jumps between days.
help.restore.step1: Click Checkpoints (the clock) in the toolbar, or press ⌘⇧T.
help.restore.step2: Scroll or drag to move, pinch or ⌘+ ⌘− to zoom, ⌘F to search. Click a card for a closer look and its notes.
help.restore.step3: Click Go Back to This. Windows returns to exactly how it was at that moment.
help.restore.note.title: What happens to now
help.restore.note.body: What Windows is doing now is replaced, unless you choose Save Current First when it asks. If Windows is off, it starts again from the checkpoint.
help.restore.fig.browse.label: Browse
help.restore.fig.browse.alt: The Checkpoints view: Now at the bottom, each day's checkpoints above it, and the timeline down the right edge
help.restore.fig.goBack.label: Go back
help.restore.fig.goBack.alt: A selected checkpoint with its larger screenshot, its notes and the Go Back to This button
help.agent.lead: Add winvm to Claude, and Claude can see the screen, use the mouse and keyboard, and run commands in Windows. Windows has to be running.
help.agent.step1: Click Use with Claude in the toolbar.
help.agent.step2: Click Add next to Claude Code or Claude Desktop. Then start a new Claude Code session, or quit and reopen Claude Desktop.
help.agent.step3: Ask in plain words: “Take a screenshot of Windows and tell me what's open.”
help.agent.note.title: Claude asks first
help.agent.note.body: Claude Code and Claude Desktop ask before each tool call unless you've allowed it. Claude can run anything in Windows and copy files to and from your Mac.
help.agent.fig.claude.alt: The Use with Claude panel, listing Claude Code and Claude Desktop, each with an Add button
